objective: Move the complete bounded monthly bill read into the existing typed PostgreSQL Ledger boundary, eliminating the silent 500-row clamp and per-row tag N+1 without changing the public REST contract.

read_contract: normal Ledger list remains paginated and capped at 500 rows
monthly Ledger list requires both date bounds and returns one complete page up to 100000 rows
a monthly result above 100000 rows fails closed instead of returning a partial collection
category filters, typed row mapping, and tags share the existing Ledger repository path
tags are loaded once for the result bill ids rather than once per row
unchanged_boundaries: GET /api/bills/by-month route, query aliases, sorting, and success/result envelope
user-scoped PostgreSQL filters and category-id resolution
integer cents and frontend transaction-type projection
bill writers, transactions, schema, configuration, and frontend code
deleted_compatibility_paths: monthly handler direct pool, BillRecord, and raw PostgreSQL query dependency
rejected_expansion: UnitOfWork, cache, streaming protocol, new transaction, or second writer
unbounded monthly response or unrelated bill-detail migration

red.result: failed before implementation because the public monthly endpoint returned 500 rows instead of the 501-row bounded month

cargo_test_workspace.result: passed against a fresh temporary PostgreSQL gate database

cargo_llvm_cov_workspace.result: passed with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 against a fresh temporary PostgreSQL gate database

review.standards_axis: passed with no findings: SQL, row mapping, category resolution, and batch tags remain in DB; handlers only orchestrate; no trait, service, UnitOfWork, transaction owner, cache, or writer was added
review.spec_axis: passed with no findings: the 501-row filtered month, tags, user scope, ordering, legacy envelope, normal 500-row pagination limit, and integer-cents projection are preserved
review.test_gap: The exact above-100000 failure branch is not materialized with a 100001-row integration fixture because that would make every workspace and coverage run allocate the maximum response; the bounded check is explicit and the residual is retained rather than hidden.
review.residual_risk: A valid month approaching 100000 rows remains an intentionally large in-memory response; pagination or streaming beyond that product boundary is a separate slice.

verification.money_review: No conversion was added or moved: database, typed Ledger, HTTP DTO, and tests remain integer cents.
verification.delivery_evidence: The Gitea PR and exact-head Actions record remain the authoritative external delivery evidence, so their immutable run identifiers are not written into the head they verify.

environment_diagnostics: An exploratory full HTTP lib run against the long-lived development database failed during test setup with sqlx VersionMismatch(25); C7j focused contracts had already passed and no monthly code path failed.
The unchanged HTTP lib suite passed 246 of 246 when run serially against a fresh temporary PostgreSQL database, proving the earlier result was stale migration state rather than a source regression.
Full workspace tests and coverage used their own fresh temporary databases and serial test threads; no source, test, or threshold was relaxed.

environment_hygiene.long_lived_development_database: not migrated, cleared, or used by passing full gates
environment_hygiene.test_database_strategy: required PostgreSQL contracts create, migrate, and remove isolated databases; the full test and coverage commands each used and removed a dedicated temporary base database
environment_hygiene.secrets: the test database URL is passed only through process environment and is not persisted in this artifact
